01_conservation.principle: a transfer moves units, never creates them: opening + receipts - served - out - expired = closing at every location

02_no_double_count.principle: one unit protects one place: both branches cannot draw the same central unit

03_unreachable_inventory.principle: stock four periods away serves nothing in the next four periods, in the plan and in the settlement

04_05_transfer_cost_monotone.principle: all else equal, a cheaper lane is used weakly more and a dearer lane weakly less

06_shorter_lead_more_useful.principle: reachable pooled stock is weakly more useful when the lane is shorter

09_shared_central_inventory.principle: total allocations cannot exceed the stock the origin holds

10_supply_cap.principle: a shared supplier capacity cannot be allocated twice across destinations

11_single_node_identity.principle: one node, no lane: the P2 fields change nothing; the canonical regression proves the frozen fixtures separately

12_zero_lane_identity.principle: disconnected nodes cannot exchange inventory: central stock serves nobody

13_14_pooling_and_correlation.principle: 13: pooling can reduce the inventory needed for the same service under independent demand; 14: the scenario worlds and the solve invent no diversification under perfect correlation

15_no_action.principle: an efficient state produces no unnecessary transfer or purchase

16_service_not_overridden.principle: a free lane never buys one branch's service with another's: every floor holds in the solve

17_allocation.explanation: central holds 80 of A against requests of 401. north receives 80 because its customers carry the higher priority (3); south receives 0.
17_allocation.principle: scarce stock goes first to the higher-priority branch and the reason is stated

18_recovery.principle: after the imbalance is recovered, transfers settle to what demand needs and never reverse

19_terminal_edge_and_loops.principle: no horizon-edge transfer spike and no loop through a priced reverse lane

20_accounting.principle: node + lane + upstream + network economics reconcile to the settlement total
